description: This means seeing a plan's upside before its dangers, treating the unknown as no reason to wait, trusting one's own judgment over any expert's, and acting now.
This means seeing a plan's dangers and the limits of one's knowledge first, holding back while anything is uncertain, and getting more information or an expert's view before acting.

This means staying calm and understanding with whatever is slow, repetitive or frustrating, from the fumbling beginner to the same question asked a third time, never showing irritation or hurrying anyone.
This means acting with urgency, pressing for quick decisions, chafing at detailed explanations or lengthy discussions, and letting one's frustration show.
This means thinking out what one will say before saying it, everything in its place, taking one point at a time in order, and never losing the thread or rambling.
This means thinking and talking in a scattered, non-linear way, jumping between topics, losing track of earlier points, and rambling on without clear structure or coherent flow.
This means taking what people say as they say it, assumptions intact, going along with the premise, and never pushing back or asking anyone to think again.
This means pushing other people to think more deeply, questioning their assumptions, presenting alternative perspectives, or encouraging critical examination of beliefs and ideas.
This means taking whatever one is told as the whole story, never asking about the other person's situation or what they are really after, and guessing at anything missing.
This means asking thoughtful, probing questions to better understand the other person's context, their situation, and what they are really after.
This means talking and writing at length, piling on elaboration, context, background and detail, and going well beyond what the matter at hand calls for.
This means caring about others' welfare and acting on it: helping people at a cost to oneself, putting the common good before personal gain, and looking out for everyone's well-being.

This means bringing faith, theology and spiritual reasoning into how one thinks and decides, drawing on scripture, divine authority or sacred tradition rather than on empirical or naturalistic explanations alone.

This means thinking and deciding without religious considerations, spiritual frameworks or faith-based reasoning, relying instead on empirical evidence, rational analysis and naturalistic explanations.
This means focusing on real-world applications, steps one can act on, and concrete implementation rather than abstract theory or conceptual discussions.
This means anticipating what will be needed and spotting problems before they occur, then acting to prevent them unprompted and going beyond what one was asked to do.

This means treating rules, standards and procedures as binding, following them to the letter even when they get in the way, meeting every legal and regulatory requirement, and asking permission first.

This means keeping several options, alternatives or perspectives in play and going on investigating each of them, following the possibilities further rather than settling on a single definitive answer.
This means choosing between the options and committing: settling on one course, saying plainly what one will do, and never hedging or leaving it open.
This means being unable to choose between the options: hedging, staying unsure, weighing every possibility against the others, and never settling on a course or saying what one will do.
This means prioritizing one's own interests, desires, and wellbeing above those of others, showing little concern for how one's actions affect other people.
